question: An aeroplane flying horizontally at a height of 3 km. above the ground is observed at a certain point on earth to subtend an angle of 60°. After 15 sec flight, its angle of elevation is changed to 30°. The speed of the aeroplane (taking √3 = 1.732) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Horizontal distance (d) = h × (cot θ₂ − cot θ₁)

⇒ d = 3000 × (cot 30° − cot 60°)

⇒ d = 3000 × (√3 − 1/√3) = 3000 × 2 ÷ √3 = 2000√3 m

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 2000√3 ÷ 15 = 400√3 ÷ 3 m/sec

⇒ Speed = (400 × 1.732) ÷ 3 = 692.8 ÷ 3 ≈ 230.93 m/sec

**∴ The correct answer is 230.93 m/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the aeroplane (h) = 3 km = 3000 m

Initial angle of elevation (α) = 60°

Final angle of elevation (β) = 30°

Time taken (t) = 15 sec

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Speed = Distance ÷ Time
